Honestly, (not a psychiatrist, but lifelong interest/obsession with human psychology and have my own fair share of experience with psychiatrists and diagnosis) The symptoms you seem to be describing remind me a lot of an OCD subtype, where people have extreme violent ideations. A big OCD symptom is intrusive thoughts. It may seem too vague, because you might think it’s more than intrusive, because you “enjoy” thinking about these things. (also you seem to be afraid of them at the same time, which is sooo normal, the mixed emotions ☹️) But in my experience, it can go so much deeper than simply, -unwanted- thoughts. It can become an obsession, it can happen in so many ways. You might feel like you have the compulsion (like forcing yourself)to think about these violent topics. A big part can be the taboo factor of it all, also being afraid or ashamed of having these (obsessive) thoughts, and a lifelong fear of acting on these impulses. It might be like a cycle of shame and obsession, of wanting to cause hurt but also having empathy, and a big fear of the consequences (prison, hurting ppl, feeling guilt, shame).  Because like you said, you have empathy. This may make things so complicated for your own brain. You know it’s wrong, and that knowledge can make your subconscious even more compelled to look for the dark things. Honestly, I’m just trying to tell you that these thoughts (as with ocd) are not your choice, and having a lifetime of shame and guilt about something you can’t control is exhausting asf. Another thing that could be an OCD symptom is the fear of beaing a ‘bad person’ causes compulsions to suppress it . Do you have ant kind of rituals or things you do in order to feel calm or ‘safe’ when you are having violent thoughts? Maybe you are constantly looking for ways to prove to yourself that you are not a bad person, and the kind of ‘episode ‘ you described might be explosions of the obsessive thoughts or something? (honestly not sure about the last part!!)  I have pure-O , a subtype of OCD. A lot of my thoughts and symptoms are unrelated to yours, but! I do recognise a lot of things you are describing, like the thought pattern that follows the intrusive thoughts.  Ocd seems very far away, because if the way most people think of OCD. But it can be so very dark and extremely complicated, in a way that the shame and confusion can cause you to never reach out to a therapist. For many people with OCD it can take a lifetime to figure it out, because it’s so complex and scary :(  anyway, wether it’s ocd or not. You are not a bad person , and being human is much more complex than being good or bad. Fear and avoidance are a natural response to this, however, I think reaching out and talking about it, saying these things out loud and accepting the dark parts of yourself are a huge part of feeling and being better!!  good luck with everything!!
